subject.title: fix(reef): repeated relay reconnects no longer leave stale sockets active

question: Should Reef forcibly terminate a failed production WebSocket after five seconds while still waiting for its real `close` event before reconnecting?
rationale: The patch supplies focused tests and near-real proof, but choosing a fixed production teardown bound is an availability-policy decision that code review cannot infer from existing public contracts.

options.title: Accept the bounded close
options.body: Approve the five-second termination bound after a refreshed current-main review, retaining the real-close ordering asserted by the lifecycle tests.

options.title: Keep graceful-close only
options.body: Do not land the forced-termination path if Reef should permit an unbounded peer close handshake instead of prioritizing reconnection availability.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded close
recommendation.body: Approve the five-second termination bound after a refreshed current-main review, retaining the real-close ordering asserted by the lifecycle tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline provides the only concrete maintainer-side routing signal through repeated mentions and subscriptions during this review.
